rule: Definition: Question Formation & Interrogative Structures (ሕቶኣዊ መዋቕራትን ኣሰራርዓኦምን) refers to the syntactic rules governing the creation of direct and indirect questions, including yes/no questions, Wh-questions, subject vs. object questions, and embedded clauses, utilizing auxiliary inversion and precise word order.

English interrogative structures are fundamentally divided into direct questions ($$\text{Direct Questions}$$) and indirect or embedded questions ($$\text{Indirect Questions}$$). To signal a direct question, English strictly requires grammatical inversion, where the auxiliary verb is placed before the subject ($$\text{Auxiliary} + \text{Subject} + \text{Verb}$$), or the introduction of a dummy auxiliary. body: Definition: Question Formation & Interrogative Structures (ሕቶኣዊ መዋቕራትን ኣሰራርዓኦምን) refers to the syntactic rules governing the creation of direct and indirect questions, including yes/no questions, Wh-questions, subject vs. object questions, and embedded clauses, utilizing auxiliary inversion and precise word order.

English interrogative structures are fundamentally divided into direct questions ($$\text{Direct Questions}$$) and indirect or embedded questions ($$\text{Indirect Questions}$$). To signal a direct question, English strictly requires grammatical inversion, where the auxiliary verb is placed before the subject ($$\text{Auxiliary} + \text{Subject} + \text{Verb}$$), or the introduction of a dummy auxiliary. Tigrinya, co

Direct Yes/No questions require the syntactic pattern $$\text{Auxiliary} + \text{Subject} + \text{Verb} \dots ?$$. In the simple present and simple past tenses, where no auxiliary is naturally present in active declarative clauses, English inserts the dummy auxiliary "do" ($$\text{Do/Does/Did} + \text{Subject} + \text{V}_{\text{base}}$$). A common error on national exams is failing to return the main verb to its base

cards.q: Could you please tell me what time ________ from the regional airport tomorrow morning?

questions.q: Could you please tell me what time ________ from the regional airport tomorrow morning?
questions.label: 1. Could you please tell me what time ________ from the regiona
why: This is an indirect (embedded) question introduced by the polite phrase 'Could you please tell me'. It requires declarative word order: $$\text{Wh-word (what time)} + \text{Subject (the flight)} + \text{Verb (departs)}$$.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q: Why ________ your science project on time last Friday, as the teacher requested?
questions.label: 2. Why ________ your science project on time last Friday, as th
why: This is a direct past Wh-question. It requires the past dummy auxiliary 'didn't' to precede the subject 'you', and the main verb must return to its base form: $$\text{Why} + \text{didn't} + \text{Subject} + \text{V}_{\text{base}}$$.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q: ________ the rare historical manuscript from the library archive last week?
questions.label: 3. ________ the rare historical manuscript from the library arc
why: This is a subject question asking about the person who performed the action of stealing. In English subject questions, no auxiliary do-support ('did') is used, and the verb remains in its past simple form ($$\text{Who/What} + \text{V}_2 + \text{Object}$$
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q: I wonder whether ________ ready to present their research findings to the board.
questions.label: 4. I wonder whether ________ ready to present their research fi
why: This is an embedded Yes/No question introduced by 'I wonder'. It requires the complementizer 'whether' followed by declarative word order: $$\text{whether} + \text{Subject} + \text{Verb}$$.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q: ________ were you talking to when the school director walked into the biology lab?
questions.label: 5. ________ were you talking to when the school director walked
why: The preposition 'to' is stranded at the end of the clause ('talking to'). In informal/standard English, when the preposition is stranded, the subjective pronoun 'Who' is used at the beginning of the question.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q: Can you tell me how long ________ as a teacher in this regional high school?
questions.label: 6. Can you tell me how long ________ as a teacher in this regio
why: This is an indirect question introduced by 'Can you tell me'. It requires declarative word order: $$\text{Wh-word (how long)} + \text{Subject (Aster)} + \text{Verb (has been working)}$$.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q: ________ did you invite to speak at the national graduation ceremony next month?
questions.label: 7. ________ did you invite to speak at the national graduation
why: This is an object question asking about the person receiving the invitation. In formal English, the objective pronoun 'Whom' is used when asking about the object of a verb.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q: Do you know ________ the main administrative office is temporarily closed today?
questions.label: 8. Do you know ________ the main administrative office is tempo
why: This is an indirect question introduced by 'Do you know'. It requires declarative word order, so the Wh-word 'why' must be followed directly by the subject 'the main administrative office'.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q: ________ of these two biology reference books do you recommend for the exam preparation?
questions.label: 9. ________ of these two biology reference books do you recomme
why: The question asks for a choice between a limited, specific group ('these two biology reference books'). This requires the selective question word 'Which'.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q: To ________ should I address this formal letter of application for the scholarship?
questions.label: 10. To ________ should I address this formal letter of applicati
why: The preposition 'To' is fronted to the beginning of the question. In formal English, a fronted preposition must strictly be followed by the objective pronoun 'whom': $$\text{Preposition} + \text{whom} \dots$$
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.
